description.p: Rostrum splits your game, voice chat, mic, music, alerts and desktop audio into named buses. Each bus goes to your headphones, to the stream, or to both, and OBS records the stream mix. It is a mixing desk, not a patchbay: faders, meters, mute and solo, and scenes you can switch live, with the PipeWire graph kept out of sight.

ul.li: Buses for game, voice, mic, music, alerts and desktop audio, each with a fader and mute
Two mixes from one console: what you hear and what your audience hears
Sets up OBS in one click and can undo every change
Optional mic filters remove background noise, cut rumble and even out your level, for the stream and every app
Check Mic plays your stream mic back in your headphones and says if the level is right
Shows when OBS is live or recording, and warns when a stream starts with the mic muted
Global shortcuts, push to talk and panic mute, plus a command line and D-Bus for Stream Deck buttons
Scenes recall every level, mute and destination, from the header or a global shortcut
Recognised apps find their bus on their own, and remember it at the next login
Audio keeps flowing if Rostrum quits or crashes

description.p: Rostrum needs PipeWire 1.0 or newer with WirePlumber 0.5 or newer. Mic filters need PipeWire 1.4 or newer.

screenshot.caption: The Mixer: Headphones and Stream masters, then a strip for each bus
The Apps page: what is playing now, and the saved rules
The OBS page: what OBS records right now
The Mic Filters page: presets, who gets the filtered mic, and Check Your Mic

description.p: First release: buses, two mixes, scenes, OBS setup and live status, mic filters and mic check, global shortcuts and remote control, automatic app assignment, undo, a compact window, private crash reports and updates.

Stream readiness checks show controls, devices, routing and observed OBS captures with scoped results and expandable evidence. Live output exclusions and microphone delivery across PipeWire quantum changes are fixed and validated in isolated audio sessions.
The x86_64 AppImage was validated on Ubuntu 26.04 with glibc 2.43, PipeWire 1.6.2 and WirePlumber 0.5.13. Compatibility with other environments is not established.
